text:
alex-customer: Hey team — started getting 401 invalid_api_key for all requests from our EU server this morning. Calls from our US infra still work. Example curl we run from eu:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
Response: {"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key is invalid or expired"}}

We didn't rotate keys. Any clues?

maria-support: Sorry you're hitting this, alex. Can you confirm if the request is going to the global host (api.redwood.com) or a region-specific host? Also paste the exact value of the `Host` and any `x-redwood-region` / `X-Forwarded-For` headers (redact the key).

alex-customer: Host: api.redwood.com
x-redwood-region: eu-west-1 (we set this header in our request routing layer)
user-agent: our-app/1.2.3

maria-support: Thanks. Quick note: we recently started enforcing region-bound API keys for some enterprise contracts — keys created under a US-only org will be rejected if the request is evaluated as coming from EU unless routed through cross-region mapping. Can you check your key metadata in the Console (Settings → API keys) and tell me the assigned region?

alex-customer: Console shows region: us-central. Hmm, our infra is multiregion but we thought the header would be enough.

dan-engineer: tagging in a quick explain: keys can be scoped to a region at creation time. If a key is region-scoped, the control plane will validate the origin region against the key metadata. Setting `x-redwood-region` doesn't override the region binding unless you have the Cross-Region Allowlist feature enabled for your org. The usual fixes are:
- use the regional endpoint (e.g. https://eu-api.redwood.com/v1) with the same key (if the key is multi-region) OR
- create a new key in the Console with region set to EU OR
- request org-level cross-region allowlist from support if you need US keys to be accepted from EU infra.

maria-support: Alex — can you try switching to the eu endpoint as a quick repro? Example:
```bash
curl -X POST https://eu-api.redwood.com/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test from eu"}'
```
If that returns 401 too, please paste the full response headers (we need the `x-rw-error-code` and `x-rw-key-region` headers).

alex-customer: Tried eu-api, same 401. Response headers:
x-rw-error-code: invalid_api_key
x-rw-key-region: us-central
x-rw-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d

maria-support: That confirms the control plane sees your key as us-central so it's rejecting EU-region requests. I'll escalate to infra to confirm there isn't an unexpected routing rule. Dan, can you review whether cross-region allowlist is enabled for this org id 98765?

dan-engineer: Looking now. I see key metadata: {"id":"sk_live_XXXX","region":"us-central","created_by":"alex@cust.com"} — no cross-region flag. Ops: we can either flip a per-key multi-region flag (requires org approval) or ask the customer to create an EU-scoped key. Which is quicker for them?

alex-customer: We prefer not to create a new key if we can avoid it — we have long-lived secrets in several environments. Is there a temporary workaround (proxying through US)?

infra-oncall: ops-bot here — proxying traffic through US infra will work but will add latency and may violate data residency rules. We can enable cross-region for this specific key after verifying business justification and updating the audit trail. If you want the enablement route, please confirm with your security contact and we'll open the change request.

maria-support: Alex, if you confirm you want us to enable cross-region for sk_live_XXXX, reply here with approval and the security owner email. Otherwise create a new key in Console: Create Key → Region: EU → copy value into your EU env (remember to rotate apps away from the old key).

alex-customer: OK — confirming to enable cross-region for sk_live_XXXX. Security contact is sec@cust.com. Please proceed.

maria-support: Got it. I've opened an internal change (CHG-2026-314) and tagged infra-oncall. Expect 1-2 hours for validation + audit logging. We'll post back when it's done.

(1 hour later)

infra-oncall: Cross-region flag enabled for sk_live_XXXX and change logged. Please retry your eu-api call.

alex-customer: Retried, and it's green ✅ responses are 200. Latency is OK. Thanks everyone!

maria-support: Glad that's resolved — closing the thread, but keeping the change visible in the audit. If you want, we can issue a new EU-scoped key so you can rotate out the old one on your schedule. :white_check_mark:
